requirements:
Implement in Rust as a SINGLE source file that compiles with rustc --edition 2024, std only. Output ONLY the Rust source code inside ```rust fences. All listed API items must be pub. Do not use inner attributes or inner documentation comments. 

Exact public API (derive Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq on the enums/structs):
pub enum RomanCase { Upper, Lower }
pub enum RomanError { Empty, InvalidByte { index: usize }, MixedCase { index: usize }, NonCanonical { index: usize }, Range }
pub fn roman_encode(value: u32, case: RomanCase) -> Result<String, RomanError>;
pub fn roman_decode(input: &str) -> Result<u32, RomanError>;

R1. roman_encode accepts 0 through 3999 inclusive; larger values return Range.
R2. Zero encodes as N in Upper case and n in Lower case.
R3. Positive values use the descending greedy tokens M=1000, CM=900, D=500, CD=400, C=100, XC=90, L=50, XL=40, X=10, IX=9, V=5, IV=4, I=1.
R4. Upper produces uppercase tokens; Lower produces their ASCII lowercase equivalents.
R5. roman_decode accepts both cases but never a mixture. Its input is not trimmed.
R6. Empty input returns Empty.
R7. All positions are zero-based UTF-8 byte offsets, including positions in non-ASCII input.
R8. Allowed bytes are exactly IVXLCDMNivxlcdmn. Scan the entire input first; the first other byte returns InvalidByte.
R9. After the allowed-byte scan, the first alphabetic byte determines the case. The first byte of the other case returns MixedCase.
R10. InvalidByte takes precedence over MixedCase regardless of where those problems occur.
R11. Exactly N or n decodes to zero.
R12. Any other input containing N or n returns NonCanonical { index: 0 }, after lexical and case checks.
R13. For N-free input compute a provisional value left to right: if the next symbol is larger, consume those two symbols and add next-current; otherwise consume one and add its value. Repeat until exhausted.
R14. If the provisional value exceeds 3999, return Range before checking canonical spelling. Saturating the provisional sum at 4000 is equivalent and permitted.
R15. For a provisional value within range, encode it using R3 and the input case. The input must equal that spelling exactly.
R16. Non-equal spelling returns NonCanonical at the first differing byte, or at the shorter length if one string is a prefix of the other.
R17. Consequently only IV, IX, XL, XC, CD and CM are canonical subtractive pairs; I, X and C repeat at most three times, M at most three times, and V, L and D never repeat.
R18. All error precedence is Empty, InvalidByte, MixedCase, N-combination, Range, canonical comparison. Both functions are deterministic and keep no state.
